title: tk factory deploy: tolerate secret propagation and resolve local wrangler
description:
Found by the first two live deploys against a real Cloudflare account. Both reported failure on deployments that were actually fine.

1. VERIFICATION RACES SECRET PROPAGATION. Order is: wrangler deploy, then secret put (which creates a new Worker version), then verify. Propagation takes roughly 10-30s, so the verify probe hits the previous version and reports 'the FACTORY_TOKEN_HASH secret did not land'. This fires on essentially every deploy — a command that always reports failure trains the operator to ignore it. Retry the verification with bounded backoff (and treat Cloudflare edge error 1042, observed during propagation, as retryable) before declaring failure. Keep the existing 'nothing is lost, re-run it' wording for genuine failure.

2. WRANGLER RESOLUTION MISSES THE REPO'S OWN COPY. There is no global wrangler in this repo; it is a devDependency of cloud/factory. Resolution tries the global binary then npx, and both fail from the repo root, so the command exits with 'a logged-in wrangler is required'. It only worked after manually putting cloud/factory/node_modules/.bin on PATH. Also probe the staged bundle dir and the repo's cloud/factory/node_modules/.bin. Keep the no-implicit-install rule.

Do not weaken the fail-closed behaviour: an unverifiable deploy must still exit nonzero after the retries are exhausted.

2026-08-19 16:49 - runner-state: substrate=herdr kind=codex branch=tick/wf0 worktree=/Users/peterengelbrecht/.herdr/worktrees/ticks/tick-wf0 workspace=wA9 base=643def4de055bf58f4190dd7bbfc181e47dc52e1 agent=tick-wf0 pane=wA9:p1 session=01a01a7f-6fc7-7971-a5f1-0d4b375f70a5
2026-08-19 17:16 - GATE FAILURE after merge — the live deploy still fails from the repo root, and the cause is a false-positive probe, not the candidate list.

Reproduced in-process: findWrangler resolves to 'npx --no wrangler' and probeVersion returns SUCCESS with version '11.13.0'. That is npm's version, not wrangler's (wrangler is 4.124.0). 'npx --no wrangler --version' exits 0 and prints npx's own version even when no wrangler is installed, so the npx candidate is accepted before the repo-local candidate is ever tried, and the deploy then dies at requireAuth with 'a logged-in wrangler is required'.

This is the repo's own documented green-start trap one layer down: a cleanly-succeeding probe that did no work. probeVersion trusts an exit code and never checks WHAT answered.

Fix: probeVersion must verify the responder is actually wrangler — assert the '--version' output identifies wrangler (and/or parse a plausible wrangler version) and reject the candidate otherwise, so resolution falls through to the next one. Add a regression test with a fake npx-shaped binary that exits 0 and prints an unrelated version: resolution must skip it and land on the repo-local wrangler.

Verified facts for the fix: the repo-local candidate itself is fine — /Users/.../cloud/factory/node_modules/.bin/wrangler --version prints 4.124.0 and whoami exits 0 from both the repo root and the staged bundle dir. Only the ordering plus the unvalidated npx probe is wrong.
2026-08-19 17:28 - Round-3 gate failure, diagnosed precisely. The probe validation itself is CORRECT — verified live: 'tk factory deploy' from the repo root now resolves 'cloud/factory/node_modules/.bin/wrangler 4.124.0, authenticated', reuses D1/R2, and completes with 'verified ... and one authenticated request', EXIT=0. The propagation retry works too.

The only failure is TestDeployResolvesWranglerThroughNpx (deploy_test.go:516), and it is a path-ordering bug introduced by the new chdir guard, not a regression in the resolver:

  restore := chdir(t, t.TempDir())                                   // line ~488 — cwd is now a temp dir
  fakeNpx, _ := filepath.Abs(filepath.Join("testdata", "fake-npx.sh"))  // line ~493 — resolves against the TEMP dir

Because the abs paths are computed AFTER the chdir, 'testdata/fake-npx.sh' resolves to <tmpdir>/testdata/fake-npx.sh, which does not exist. The symlinks are therefore dangling, npx cannot exec, every candidate fails, and Deploy returns the 'wrangler is required' PrerequisiteError.

Fix: resolve both filepath.Abs(...) values BEFORE the chdir (or capture the package dir first and join against it). The chdir guard itself is right and should stay — it is what stops the repo's own dependency from winning in a checkout.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy against a real account (or a harness that simulates propagation lag by returning 503/1042 for the first N probes) verifies successfully instead of failing; exhausted retries still exit nonzero with the existing actionable message; wrangler resolves without the operator adjusting PATH when only cloud/factory has it installed; scripts/verify-factory-deploy.sh still passes all scenarios.
